name: Mushi
overview: Mushi is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified uniquely as the son of Merari. He is associated with the Mushites, a group named after him, indicating his role as a progenitor within the Levitical clan. His lineage is significant within the Levitical genealogy, emphasizing his place in the priestly tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Mushi appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine attribution. It is simply recorded as the name of this Levitical figure in Exodus 6:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mushi as the son of Merari. Additionally, there are inferred relationships linking him to Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth as ancestors, suggesting a broader genealogical context within the Levitical families as noted in 1 Chronicles 6:47 and 23:23.
scriptureSignificance: Mushi's importance lies in his role as a son of Merari, one of the chief families of the Levites, which were set apart for service to God. The Mushites, derived from his name, represent a distinct Levitical clan, underscoring the organized structure God established for the priestly duties. His mention in the genealogies highlights the faithful transmission of Levitical heritage vital for the worship and service of the Lord.
